name: Zhang Min
current_role: Chairman and President, Cofoe Medical Technology (301087.SZ / 01187.HK), Changsha
profile: Zhang Min (b. 1979, CSU EMBA) co-founded Changsha-based Cofoe with his wife Nie Juan, starting with 'Hao Hushi' home-medical stores in 2007 and launching the Cofoe brand in 2009. Cofoe makes home medical devices (monitoring, rehab, respiratory, TCM therapy, hearing) and became the first home-medical-device maker listed in both Shenzhen (A) and Hong Kong (H).
interesting_fact: Cofoe runs 600+ self-operated stores, sells through 200,000+ pharmacies and owns brands such as Beibeijia posture correctors and Jian'er Hearing (689 hearing-aid centres in 135 cities).
deep_cut_fact: The name is deliberate: Chinese 'Kefu' (可孚) draws on the classical gloss '孚，信也' ('fu' means trust), while the English 'Cofoe' comes from 'Comfortable'.
notes: Shares listing with wife Nie Juan (former vice-chair). No personal public profile; IR inbox is the best route. Background via 36kr citing prospectus: https://36kr.com/p/3797203049591561

name: Lu Shenglin
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong OPT Machine Vision Tech Co. (688686.SH), Dongguan (per third-party exec data; latest status unverified)
profile: Lu Shenglin, who holds a PhD in machinery manufacturing and automation, co-founded OPT in Dongguan in 2006 with his brother Lu Zhilin (now general manager). OPT makes machine-vision lighting, lenses, cameras and software for electronics and battery manufacturing and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He has been chairman and R&D director since May 2018.
interesting_fact: OPT has a global footprint unusual for a Chinese vision firm, with offices in Cupertino (California), Stuttgart, Tokyo, Penang, Bangkok and Vietnam.
notes: The Forbes bio says HQ is Wuxi, but the company's own site and filings put it in Dongguan, Guangdong. optmv@optmv.com is the company's general inbox (not IR-specific). Brothers Lu Shenglin and Lu Zhilin are joint actual controllers. Role source: https://www.lixinger.com/equity/company/detail/sh/688686/688686/senior-executive/shareholding-compensation

name: Christopher Urmson
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aurora Innovation (NASDAQ: AUR)
profile: Canadian roboticist Chris Urmson led CMU's DARPA Grand/Urban Challenge teams, then spent 2009-2016 at Google's self-driving project (later Waymo), becoming project lead and CTO. In 2017 he co-founded Aurora with Sterling Anderson and Drew Bagnell. Aurora launched commercial driverless trucking in Texas in 2025 and is targeting 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030.
interesting_fact: He was technical director of the Carnegie Mellon 'Boss' team that won the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge. CMU vehicles also took 2nd and 3rd in the 2005 Grand Challenge.
deep_cut_fact: His 2005 CMU PhD thesis, 'Navigation Regimes for Off-Road Autonomy' (co-chaired by Red Whittaker), split off-road driving into efficiency-, stop- and swerve-limited regimes and cited planetary exploration and mine-mapping as low-speed cases.
notes: Born 1976 in Canada to English emigrant parents. Grew up in Trenton ON, Victoria BC, Winnipeg and Saskatoon. BSc in computer engineering, University of Manitoba, 1998. Highly relevant to tech/AI podcasts and a frequent public speaker; Aurora's press office is the best route.

name: Chi Jinhua
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Wu Xidun) of Tonze New Energy Technology Co. (002759.SZ), Shantou. Holds no listed executive title.
profile: Chi Jinhua and her husband Wu Xidun (the chairman) control Shantou-based Tonze, founded in 1996 as a small-appliance maker known for ceramic electric stew pots and health kettles. After listing in 2015 and fully acquiring Jiangsu Xintai Materials in 2016, it became mainly a maker of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6), the electrolyte salt in lithium-ion batteries, and renamed itself Tonze New Energy.
interesting_fact: An energy-transition pivot: in 2024 Tonze earned about RMB 1.5bn from LiPF6 and fluorochemicals, versus only about RMB 208m from the kitchen appliances it was built on.
notes: Very low public profile and no executive role; husband Wu Xidun (chairman) is the public face. zwl@tonze.com is the board secretary's (Zheng Wenlong) published disclosure email in the 2024 annual report. Off the Hurun list since 2021. 'Alive' is not confirmed by any source; she is still named as actual controller in the 2024 annual report.

name: Zhou Zhiqun
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and CFO, Shenzhen Forms Syntron Information Co. (300468.SZ)
profile: Zhou Zhiqun co-founded Shenzhen Forms Syntron in November 2003 with former colleague Deng Xiusheng. The firm builds core-banking, payments and fintech software, largely for Hong Kong and Macau banks, and has worked on blockchain projects. He became sole actual controller in 2018 and took back the general manager role in 2024; the company is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Forms Syntron filed for an H-share listing in Hong Kong but postponed the global offering in September 2026, citing market conditions.
